title: A category added by the shop gets an empty row
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure AccountingHub is enabled for the organization and the test location has no QuickBooks Online connection.
custom_steps:
1. Open Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders.
  2. Click "New No Charge Category".
  3. Type a new name in Name.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Open Accounting > Account Mappings.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The categories page opens.

Step 2:

  • The window opens.

Step 3:

  • The name shows.

Step 4:

  • The category is listed.

Step 5:

  • A new row "No Charge: [new name]" shows, empty; it is not filled from another row.

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11763 (Story 6, AccountingHub account mapping)

  • S6-R1: “Accounting > Account Mappings shows one row per category under "Parts cost of goods sold", named after the category ("Internal: General Internal", "No Charge: Warranty"), each a picker over the organization's chart of accounts like the other rows. A category the shop adds appears as a new empty row; an archived category keeps its row and can still be remapped, so a held entry of that category can post. The shop supplies amount of Story 10 is credited to the existing "Shop supplies expense" row; no new row for it. An empty row holds the event (S8-N2); there is no fallback to another row. Same model as S5-R6: the row lives on the category, archiving keeps it, Restore brings it back.”
  • S6-R2: “Automatically set up the starting category mappings using AccountingHub's existing chart of accounts. General Internal defaults to 6500 Vehicle Expenses, already in the default chart. Warranty and Goodwill both default to 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense, already in the newer chart. Comeback defaults to 6440 Comeback Expense, a new required account (number confirmed by the AccountingHub owner on 2026-11-09). The existing 6400 Shop Equipment Maintenance account remains available for accountants to select where appropriate; it is not an additional starting category. The mapping key should allow a kind (parts, labor) later, so V2 adds rows instead of changing the contract.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
